chunks: Or do they say: 'We are a well-accoutred army?'
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about the disbelievers' claim of being a victorious army in Surah Al-Qamar?
ai.summary: In the context of Surah Al-Qamar, this verse challenges the polytheists of Mecca who believed their numerical superiority and tribal cohesion guaranteed victory against the Prophet Muhammad. Shia exegetes often view this as a critique of worldly arrogance, emphasizing that true victory belongs to those who align with divine will rather than mere human strength.
